nacl-db: The db subnet NACL is missing its inbound allow rule for tcp/3306 from the app subnets, blocking all database connections.

actions: c_role > target_health > console_a > c_rt_app_a > c_nat_a > c_sg_app > c_nacl_app > c_igw > c_rt_pub > c_nacl_pub
diagnoses: nacl-pub: Inbound rules only allow tcp/80 and tcp/443 instead of all traffic, blocking ephemeral-port return traffic for NAT gateway connections (e.g., app-tier egress to S3) and causing connect timeouts.
nacl-app: The nacl-app inbound rule for tcp/80 allows traffic from the db subnets instead of allowing from the whole VPC CIDR, so ALB health checks/traffic from the public subnets are blocked.
target-group: Target group health check path is set to /healthz instead of /health, causing the health check to 404 and all targets to be marked unhealthy.
target-group: Target group health check (and target) port is set to 8080 instead of 80, so health checks time out even though the app listens on port 80.
asg: The Auto Scaling group is not attached to the tg-app target group, so no instances register as targets behind the ALB.
alb: The ALB's port 80 listener forwards to tg-old instead of tg-app, so traffic never reaches the ASG-registered targets.

actions: target_health > c_tg > curl_localhost_health@a > read_app_logs > c_appcfg > console_a > c_lt
diagnoses: launch-template: The launch template has a health_redirect setting enabled, causing the web server to return 301 redirects instead of 200 on all paths including /health, failing ALB health checks.
alb: The ALB is configured with subnets pub-a and app-b instead of pub-a and pub-b, placing its AZ-b node in the private application subnet.
launch-template: The launch template specifies AMI ami-web-v3 which does not exist, so instances never launch and nothing registers with the target group.
asg: Auto Scaling group desired capacity is set to 0 instead of 2, so no instances are launched.

actions: target_health > curl_localhost_health@a > c_tg > c_lt > console_a > c_sg_app
diagnoses: target-group: Target group tg-app is configured to health-check and forward on port 80, but the web server actually listens on port 8080, causing all targets to fail health checks. || launch-template: Launch template configures the web server to listen on port 8080 instead of port 80, so health checks and ALB traffic on port 80 never reach the app.
asg: The Auto Scaling group's subnets are set to only app-a instead of both app-a and app-b, so both instances launch in AZ a.
iam-role: role-app is missing the s3:PutObject permission on arn:aws:s3:::assets-bkt/*, so the app cannot write uploads to S3.
iam-role: role-app's s3:GetObject/PutObject policy is scoped to arn:aws:s3:::assets-bkt instead of arn:aws:s3:::assets-bkt/*, so object-level access to config/app.json is denied.

launch-template: The launch template has no IAM instance profile attached (profile is None instead of role-app), so instances can't authenticate to SSM or S3 to fetch config/app.json, causing the web server to fail to start.

iam-role: role-app's trust policy allows lambda.amazonaws.com to assume it instead of ec2.amazonaws.com, so EC2 instances cannot obtain credentials, causing SSM registration failure and user-data config fetch failure
bucket-policy: The assets-bkt bucket policy contains an explicit Deny on s3:PutObject for role-app, overriding the IAM role's allow and causing uploads to fail.
iam-role: role-app is missing the Systems Manager agent permissions (ssm/ssmmessages/ec2messages), so instances are not managed by Systems Manager
iam-role: Role role-app is missing the logs:PutLogEvents permission needed to send application logs to CloudWatch Logs.
app-config: The app configuration in S3 stores the stale DB endpoint appdb.old instead of the current endpoint appdb.current, causing DB connections to fail with an unknown host error.
app-config: The app config in S3 stores an outdated/stale database password instead of the current RDS password, causing db-auth-failed errors.

actions: target_health > nc_rds_3306@b > read_app_logs > c_nacl_db > console_b > c_rds
diagnoses: rds: RDS instance has Multi-AZ disabled, so there is no standby to fail over to when the AZ hosting the single DB instance goes offline.
cloudfront: The default origin is set to a stale ALB domain name (alb-old) instead of the current ALB, so CloudFront cannot resolve the origin for all non-static requests.
cloudfront: The CloudFront origin for the ALB is set to https-only but the ALB only listens on HTTP:80, so CloudFront cannot connect to the origin.
bucket-policy: The bucket policy does not grant the CloudFront origin access control read access to static/, so CloudFront cannot fetch objects from assets-bkt.
